prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Look for signs of past renovations, or deviations from architectural details.
3. Go back to the inspection records.
4. Take notes. Keep them organized.
5. Ask yourself, “did I miss anything?” - If the answer to #5 is yes, then go back to step two.
6. When the inspection is over, the note taking begins. Remember, the people who will be reading your report are likely architects, engineers, or the non-accessibility specialist owner.
7. Reference drawings. Write accurately. I highly recommend using words that are technical and specific. “This is not a ramp” should be replaced with “This feature does not comply with slope requirements as defined in XYZ code.”

If you use these instructions any time soon you will have a lot of free time. You can use that free time to create 2D or 3D renderings of the barriers, site-photos for reference, and
